- [x] **T1 Repo scaffold** — every clone runs `entire enable --agent <agent>` and checks `.git/hooks/post-commit` exists; layout from CLAUDE.md, empty folders with `__init__.py`, `backend/pyproject.toml`, `frontend/` Next.js init, `notes/A.md|B.md|C.md`, `.gitignore`, `.env.example`. *(A drives, others review)*

- [x] **T3 Pick demo cases** — 3 founder-mode companies + 2 investor-mode pairs, incl. one counter-drone set (Sensofusion / Stendr / Nordic Air Defence) for the conflict moment. Write them in `contracts/fixtures/README.md`.

---

## A — Data & infra

### CP1 — Friday night (unblocks B and C)
- [x] **A1 Raw fixtures** — script `backend/data/record_fixtures.py` that calls Cala for the T3 cases and saves raw JSON to `contracts/fixtures/raw/`. Needs: T1–T3. *(Contract files: fixture data only, approved by T2.)*
- [x] **A2 Model fixtures + FakeDataStore** — mappers raw → contract models into `contracts/fixtures/models/`; `fake_store.py` implementing `DataStore` from them; `get_store()` with `USE_FAKE_STORE`. Tests: every fake method returns valid models. Needs: A1.

### CP2 — Saturday until ~15:00 (real data)
- [ ] **A3 Cala client** — `cala_client.py`: async httpx, `X-API-KEY`, retries/backoff, semaphore, timeouts, call log. Tests with mocked HTTP. Needs: T1.
- [ ] **A4 Introspection map** — fetch introspection once per entity type (Company, Organization, FundingRound, Person), cache to `backend/data/introspection.json`; helper `fields_for(type)`. Needs: A3.

- [ ] **A6 Store: resolve + company** — `CalaDataStore.resolve()` (with investor type/description guard) and `.company()`. Tests on raw fixtures. Needs: A3, A4.
- [ ] **A7 Store: rounds + investor_rounds** — via `PARTICIPATES_IN_FUNDING_ROUND` + round properties; `is_lead` from the investor edge; amount via A5. Needs: A6, A5.
- [ ] **A8 Store: portfolio + people** — `INVESTED_IN` outgoing for investors; `IS_BOARD_MEMBER_OF` / `FOUNDED` / `IS_CEO_OF` / `WORKS_AT` incoming for companies. Needs: A6.
- [ ] **A9 Store: sourced_answer** — `knowledge_search` → markdown + `Reason[]` built from `explainability` claims and `context` source URLs. Needs: A3.
- [ ] **A10 Atlas cache** — `cache/atlas.py` wraps client calls (key, 24 h TTL, `CACHE_ONLY` mode); hit/miss in the call log. Needs: A3.
- [ ] **A11 candidate_competitors v1** — `knowledge_query` on industry + Nordic/Baltic countries + adjacent stages, dedupe, exclude self. (Vector search comes in A13.) Needs: A6.
- [ ] **A12 Switch-over** — `USE_FAKE_STORE=false` works end to end for one demo company; tell B. **= CP2.** Needs: A6–A11.

### CP3/CP4 — Saturday evening & night
- [ ] **A13 Vector search** — embeddings via Verda Inference API (Gemini fallback), Atlas Vector Search index, merge into `candidate_competitors`. Needs: A11.
- [ ] **A14 Batch job: crawl** — `batch/precompute_graph.py` part 1: list active Nordic/Baltic investors, fetch portfolios + rounds into Atlas. Idempotent, resumable. Needs: A7, A8, A10.
- [ ] **A15 Batch job: derive** — part 2: `investor_graph` (co-investor counts), `investor_activity` (last lead, rounds per sector/stage). `co_investors()` reads it. Needs: A14.
- [ ] **A16 Run batch on Verda** — package as a Verda batch job, run overnight, document in `deploy/verda.md`. Needs: A15.
- [ ] **A17 Docker + deploy** — Dockerfile (API + MCP server), deploy to a Verda CPU instance with HTTPS; share URL. Needs: B10.

### CP5 — Sunday morning
- [ ] **A18 Pre-cache demo** — warm the cache for all T3 cases; verify `CACHE_ONLY=true` runs the full demo offline. Needs: A10, A17.
- [ ] **A19 Deploy notes** — finish `deploy/verda.md` (services used, why, costs, how to run). Hand to C for the README.

---

## B — Intelligence

### CP1–CP2 — Friday night & Saturday (on FakeDataStore)
- [ ] **B1 API skeleton** — `api/main.py`: FastAPI app, CORS, `/api/health`, all routes from §5.3 returning fixture-based stub responses validated by the models. Needs: T2, A2.

- [ ] **B8 Eval set** — `backend/tests/core/test_eval.py`: Kelluu → NATO Innovation Fund appears as lead; Maki.vc shows defence pre-seed leads; counter-drone conflict detected; runs on fake + real store. Needs: B6.

### CP3 — Saturday ~20:00
- [ ] **B9 Real-data pass** — run everything with `USE_FAKE_STORE=false`, fix mapping surprises (via notes to A), tune weights. Needs: A12, B8.
- [ ] **B10 Founder mode end to end** — the API serves real `FounderReport`s for the 3 demo companies under ~10 s (cached). **= CP3 with C.** Needs: B9.

### CP4 — Saturday night
- [ ] **B11 Briefs** — `core/briefs.py` + `/api/brief`: facts + `sourced_answer` claims → Gemini formats → `Brief` with citations; no uncited sentences. Needs: B10, A9.
- [ ] **B12 Agent tools** — `agent/tools.py`: tool schemas for core functions + `sourced_answer`. Needs: B10.
- [ ] **B13 Agent loop + slush-prep** — `agent/gemini_agent.py` function-calling loop (max 12 calls), job store in memory, `/api/slush-prep` + `/api/jobs/{id}/stream` SSE of `AgentEvent`s. Needs: B12, B11.
- [ ] **B14 Chat** — `/api/chat` streaming over the same loop, scoped to the current company/investor. Needs: B13.
- [ ] **B15 MCP server** — `mcp_server/server.py` with the §5.4 tools; tested in Claude Desktop alongside Cala MCP. Needs: B10.

### CP5 — Sunday morning
- [ ] **B16 Hardening** — timeouts, friendly errors, response validation everywhere, prompt tightening, final weight tune on the eval set.

## C — Product

### CP1 — Friday night
- [x] **C1 Frontend scaffold** — Next.js + TS + Tailwind, layout, `lib/types.ts` mirroring schemas, `lib/api.ts` client with `API_URL`. Needs: T1, T2.
- [x] **C2 Mock API** — `frontend/mock/` serving the §5.3 routes from `contracts/fixtures/models/` (incl. a fake SSE stream). Needs: A2, C1.

### CP2–CP3 — Saturday
- [ ] **C3 Home + resolve** — mode toggle, input, `/api/resolve`, entity confirm list (name, type, description). Needs: C2.
- [x] **C4 Source badge component** — rank label + date + link; used everywhere. Needs: C1.
- [ ] **C5 Founder report: competitors** — removable competitor chips with reason tooltips. Needs: C3.
- [ ] **C6 Founder report: Pitch + Skip lists** — investor cards (score, leads in space, last lead, warm paths, reasons with badges); Skip list shows the conflict first. Needs: C5, C4.
- [ ] **C7 Investor check screen** — conflicts, competitors + their backers, round history. Needs: C4.
- [ ] **C8 Switch to real API** — point `API_URL` at B's server, fix integration issues (via notes to B). **= CP3 with B.** Needs: B10, C6.
- [ ] **C9 Founder testing** — show C6 to 3–5 founders at Junction; record feedback + one quote in `docs/user-testing.md`.

### CP4 — Saturday night
- [ ] **C10 Brief page** — markdown render + citation list with badges. Needs: C8.
- [ ] **C11 Slush prep** — paste investor names → `/api/slush-prep` → live SSE steps → brief cards. Needs: C10 (mock SSE until B13).
- [ ] **C12 Chat panel** — streaming chat on report/brief pages. Needs: C8 (mock until B14).
- [ ] **C13 MCP demo setup** — Claude Desktop config for Cala + Pitchlist MCP; test the "Should I pitch Fund X?" question; steps in `docs/mcp-demo.md`. Needs: B15.

### CP5 — Sunday morning
- [ ] **C14 Polish** — loading / empty / error states, responsive check, copy pass.
- [ ] **C15 README + docs** — `README.md` + `docs/`: setup, architecture, how Cala / Gemini / Atlas / Verda are used (from A19). Needs: A19.
- [ ] **C16 Demo + pitch** — demo script (founder conflict → flip to investor mode → MCP in Claude Desktop), slides, rehearse twice with the team, record a backup video.

# Notes — Agent B (Intelligence)

Requests for other areas and "not yet checked against live <service>" lines go here (CLAUDE.md rules 2 and 12).

## Contract review

- **B approves contracts 1.1.0** (commit 3559ed7, 13 Nov). All B review points are covered: competitor_ids, people()/company() for investor IDs, InvestorCheck.rounds scope, chat citations, [n] markers, score 0-100, co_investors() returning [].

## Pending live checks (rule 12)

- B2: `agent/llm.structured()` not yet checked against live Gemini (no GEMINI_API_KEY yet). Check: one call with a nested contract model as schema.

## B6 scoring decision (13 Nov, agreed with human)

- **Skip** = investors with a PORTFOLIO or BOARD conflict with a *direct* competitor (the 10–15 from B3).
- **Pitch pool** = investors in rounds of the *other* candidates (similar, not judged direct)
  ∪ `co_investors()` of the company's current investors (these are also warm paths); minus everyone on Skip.
- **Rank Pitch** by leads_in_space, rounds_in_space, recency of last lead, warm paths (weights dict at the top of `core/scoring.py`).
- **No special handling for big / state funds** (e.g. Tesi). One conflict = Skip, even if they back everyone. Don't add a softer label.

# Pitchlist contracts — API, MCP tools, fixtures

Contract version: **1.1.0** (`CONTRACT_VERSION` in `contracts/schemas.py`).
**Frozen after task T2.** Changes need all three humans to agree; then bump `CONTRACT_VERSION`,
note it in `contracts/CHANGELOG.md` and update `CLAUDE.md` §5 in the same commit.

All model names below (`EntityRef`, `FounderReport`, ...) are the Pydantic models in
`contracts/schemas.py`. JSON field names are the model field names, unchanged.

## REST API — B implements, C consumes

| Method | Path | Body | Returns |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| POST | `/api/resolve` | `{name, kind}` | `EntityRef[]` |
| POST | `/api/founder/analyze` | `{company_id, competitor_ids?: string[]}` | `FounderReport` |
| POST | `/api/investor/check` | `{investor_id, company_id}` | `InvestorCheck` |
| POST | `/api/brief` | `{investor_id, company_id}` | `Brief` |
| POST | `/api/slush-prep` | `{company_id, investor_names: string[]}` | `{job_id}` |
| GET | `/api/jobs/{id}/stream` | — | SSE stream of `AgentEvent` |
| POST | `/api/chat` | `{company_id?, investor_id?, message}` | SSE stream of `AgentEvent` |
| GET | `/api/health` | — | `{ok: true, contract_version}` |

- `kind` is `"company"` or `"investor"`.
- Errors: HTTP 4xx/5xx with `{error: string}`.
- CORS open for the frontend origin.

### Rules the models can't express

- **Removing competitors (`competitor_ids`).** Without it, B finds the competitors itself. With it,
  B skips that step and ranks against exactly those company IDs. The frontend sends the IDs still
  shown after the user removed some (taken from the previous `FounderReport.competitors`).
- **Score.** `InvestorScore.score` is 0–100, higher = better fit. `pitch` and `skip` are each sorted
  by score, highest first. An investor with one or more `conflicts` is in `skip`, never in `pitch`.
- **Lead data.** `InvestorScore.lead_data` says how far `leads_in_space` can be trusted: `known`
  (every round in the space says who led), `partial` (some do), `unknown` (none do — show
  `rounds_in_space` instead and say so in the UI).
- **`InvestorCheck.rounds`** holds the rounds of `company` and of every competitor. Group them by
  `Round.company_id` to show who backed each rival.
- **Citations in briefs.** `Brief.markdown` cites with `[n]` markers; `n` is a 1-based index into
  `Brief.citations`.

### Streams (`/api/jobs/{id}/stream`, `/api/chat`)

- Wire format: one `data: <AgentEvent JSON>\n\n` per event. No named events (`event:` lines), no
  ids. The stream closes after the `done` event. `/api/chat` is a POST, so the frontend reads it
  with a streaming `fetch`, not `EventSource`.
- Event types:
  - `step` — a progress line in `message` (e.g. a tool call).
  - `text` — a chunk of the answer in `message`; append chunks in order.
  - `brief` — one finished brief in `brief`.
  - `error` — what failed, in `message`. The stream continues unless `done` follows.
  - `done` — end of the stream.
- **Slush prep:** every event about one pasted investor carries `investor_name` (the name exactly
  as pasted) and, once resolved, `investor`. A name that doesn't resolve, or matches several
  entities that can't be told apart, gets an `error` event with that `investor_name`.
- **Chat:** the answer arrives as `text` events. Its sources arrive in `citations` on the `done`
  event; `[n]` in the text is a 1-based index into that list.

## Data layer interface — A implements, B consumes

`DataStore` (a `Protocol` in `contracts/schemas.py`):

```python
class DataStore(Protocol):
    async def resolve(self, name: str, kind: Literal["company", "investor"]) -> list[EntityRef]: ...
    async def company(self, id: str) -> Company: ...
    async def rounds(self, company_id: str) -> list[Round]: ...
    async def investor_rounds(self, investor_id: str) -> list[Round]: ...
    async def portfolio(self, investor_id: str) -> list[PortfolioLink]: ...
    async def people(self, company_id: str) -> list[PersonLink]: ...
    async def candidate_competitors(self, company: Company, k: int = 30) -> list[Company]: ...
    async def co_investors(self, investor_id: str) -> list[tuple[EntityRef, int]]: ...
    async def sourced_answer(self, question: str) -> tuple[str, list[Reason]]: ...  # knowledge_search
```

`backend/data/__init__.py` exposes `get_store() -> DataStore`, returning `FakeDataStore` when
`USE_FAKE_STORE=true`, else the real store. B only ever calls `get_store()`.

- `company(id)` works for any organisation ID, including an investor.
- `people(id)` also accepts an investor ID and returns that investor's own people (then
  `PersonLink.company_id` is the investor ID). BOARD conflicts need this: a competitor's `BOARD`
  person who is also one of the investor's people.
- `co_investors(id)` returns `[]` when nothing is known yet (the precomputed graph arrives with the
  batch job, after the real store). It never raises for that.

## MCP tools — B implements (thin wrappers over core)

`resolve_company`, `find_competitors`, `get_rounds`, `investor_profile`, `check_conflict`,
`rank_investors`, `investor_brief`.

Inputs are entity IDs (plus `name` for `resolve_company`); outputs are the contract models as JSON.

- `README.md` — the demo cases (task T3).
- `raw/` — raw Cala responses (A records them; never hand-edited).
- `models/` — contract-model JSON built from raw. `FakeDataStore` reads it; C's mock API serves it.

content.content:
B skips that step and ranks against exactly those company IDs. The frontend sends the IDs still
  shown after the user removed some (taken from the previous `FounderReport.competitors`).
- **Score.** `InvestorScore.score` is 0–100, higher = better fit. `pitch` and `skip` are each sorted
  by score, highest first. An investor with one or more `conflicts` is in `skip`, never in `pitch`.
- **Lead data.** `InvestorScore.lead_data` says how far `leads_in_space` can be trusted: `known`
  (every round in the space says who led), `partial` (some do), `unknown` (none do — show
  `rounds_in_space` instead and say so in the UI).

"""Gemini wrapper (B2): one call that returns a validated Pydantic model.

Every Gemini call in core/ and agent/ goes through `structured()`. Model names come from
GEMINI_MODEL_FAST / GEMINI_MODEL_SMART, the key from GEMINI_API_KEY.
"""

import asyncio
import os
from functools import cache
from typing import Any, Literal, TypeVar

import httpx
from google import genai
from google.genai import errors, types
from pydantic import BaseModel, ValidationError

T = TypeVar("T", bound=BaseModel)

RETRY_CODES = {429, 500, 502, 503, 504}


class LLMError(RuntimeError):
    """Gemini is not configured, or no valid answer after all retries."""


def model_name(tier: Literal["fast", "smart"] = "fast") -> str:
    """Model id for a tier; `smart` falls back to the fast model when unset."""
    fast = os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL_FAST", "").strip()
    name = (os.environ.get("GEMINI_MODEL_SMART", "").strip() or fast) if tier == "smart" else fast
    if not name:
        raise LLMError("GEMINI_MODEL_FAST is not set in .env")
    return name


@cache
def _client() -> genai.Client:
    key = os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY", "").strip()
    if not key:
        raise LLMError("GEMINI_API_KEY is not set in .env")
    return genai.Client(api_key=REDACTED


async def structured(
    prompt: str,
    schema: type[T],
    *,
    system: str | None = None,
    tier: Literal["fast", "smart"] = "fast",
    retries: int = 3,
    backoff: float = 1.0,
    client: Any = None,
) -> T:

"""find_competitors (B3): the store's candidates, judged by Gemini down to the direct competitors.

Gemini only picks among candidate IDs and writes a one-line reason; any ID it invents is dropped.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pydantic import BaseModel

from agent.llm import structured
from contracts.schemas import Company, Competitor
from data import get_store

MAX_COMPETITORS = 15

SYSTEM = """You judge which companies are DIRECT competitors of a startup, for a founder deciding \
which investors to pitch (an investor who backed a direct competitor has a conflict).
A direct competitor sells a similar product or service to similar customers. Same broad industry \
alone is not enough; investors, funds, agencies and suppliers are never competitors.
Use only the descriptions given. Return at most 15, the most direct first; return fewer (or none) \
if fewer qualify. Use only IDs from the candidate list, copied exactly. Each reason is one short \
factual sentence on what overlaps, with no numbers, dates or names not in the descriptions."""


class _Pick(BaseModel):
    id: str
    reason: str


class _Judgement(BaseModel):
    competitors: list[_Pick]


def _line(c: Company) -> str:
    facts = [
        f"industries: {', '.join(c.industries)}" if c.industries else "",
        f"stage: {c.stage}" if c.stage else "",
        f"country: {c.country}" if c.country else "",
    ]
    meta = "; ".join(f for f in facts if f)
    return f"- id={c.id} | {c.name} | {c.description or 'no description'}" + (
        f" | {meta}" if meta else ""
    )


async def find_competitors(company: Company, k: int = 30) -> list[Competitor]:
    candidates = [
        c for c in await get_store().candidate_competitors(company, k) if c.id != company.id
    ]
    if not candidates:
        return []
    by_id = {c.id: c for c in candidates}
    prompt = (
        f"Startup:\n{_line(company)}\n\n"
        f"Candidates:\n" + "\n".join(_line(c) for c in by_id.values())
    )
    judged = await structured(prompt, _Judgement, system=SYSTEM)

    out: list[Competitor] = []
    for pick in judged.competitors:
        c = by_id.pop(pick.id.strip(), None)  # pop: unknown and repeated IDs are both dropped
        if c is not None:
            out.append(Competitor(company=c, reason=pick.reason.strip()))
    return out[:MAX_COMPETITORS]

"""find_competitors on the fake store with a scripted Gemini judge."""

import pytest

import core.competitors as competitors
from data import get_store

KELLUU = "78d7490a-dd04-5119-a7f1-e940b861219b"


@pytest.fixture
def store(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("USE_FAKE_STORE", "true")
    get_store.cache_clear()
    yield get_store()
    get_store.cache_clear()


def judge(picks):
    """Fake `structured`: records the prompt, answers with `picks(candidate_ids)`."""
    seen = {}

    async def fake(prompt, schema, **kw):
        seen["prompt"] = prompt
        ids = [line.split("id=")[1].split(" |")[0] for line in prompt.splitlines() if "id=" in line]
        seen["ids"] = ids
        return schema.model_validate({"competitors": picks(ids[1:])})  # ids[0] = the startup

    return fake, seen


async def test_keeps_only_candidate_ids_in_judge_order(store, monkeypatch):
    company = await store.company(KELLUU)
    fake, seen = judge(
        lambda ids: [
            {"id": ids[2], "reason": "Also sells aerial surveillance."},
            {"id": "made-up-id", "reason": "invented"},
            {"id": ids[0], "reason": "Same customers."},
            {"id": ids[2], "reason": "duplicate"},
            {"id": KELLUU, "reason": "itself"},
        ]
    )
    monkeypatch.setattr(competitors, "structured", fake)

    out = await competitors.find_competitors(company)

    assert [c.company.id for c in out] == [seen["ids"][3], seen["ids"][1]]
    assert out[0].reason == "Also sells aerial surveillance."
    assert KELLUU not in seen["ids"][1:]  # the startup is never a candidate
    assert all(c.company.sources for c in out)  # candidate Company kept whole, sources included

"""find_competitors (B3): the store's candidates, judged by Gemini down to the direct competitors.

Gemini only picks among candidate IDs and writes a one-line reason; any ID it invents is dropped.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pydantic import BaseModel

from agent.llm import structured
from contracts.schemas import Company, Competitor
from data import get_store

MAX_COMPETITORS = 15

SYSTEM = """You judge which companies are DIRECT competitors of a startup, for a founder deciding \
which investors to pitch (an investor who backed a direct competitor has a conflict).
A direct competitor sells a similar product or service to similar customers. Same broad industry \
alone is not enough; investors, funds, agencies and suppliers are never competitors.
Use only the descriptions given. Return at most 15, the most direct first; return fewer (or none) \
if fewer qualify. Use only IDs from the candidate list, copied exactly. Each reason is one short \
factual sentence on what overlaps, with no numbers, dates or names not in the descriptions."""


class _Pick(BaseModel):
    id: str
    reason: str


class _Judgement(BaseModel):
    competitors: list[_Pick]


def _line(c: Company) -> str:
    facts = [
        f"industries: {', '.join(c.industries)}" if c.industries else "",
        f"stage: {c.stage}" if c.stage else "",
        f"country: {c.country}" if c.country else "",
    ]
    meta = "; ".join(f for f in facts if f)
    return f"- id={c.id} | {c.name} | {c.description or 'no description'}" + (
        f" | {meta}" if meta else ""
    )


async def find_competitors(company: Company, k: int = 30) -> list[Competitor]:
    candidates = [
        c for c in await get_store().candidate_competitors(company, k) if c.id != company.id
    ]
    if not candidates:
        return []
    by_id = {c.id: c for c in candidates}
    prompt = (
        f"Startup:\n{_line(company)}\n\n"
        f"Candidates:\n" + "\n".join(_line(c) for c in by_id.values())
    )
    judged = await structured(prompt, _Judgement, system=SYSTEM)

    out: list[Competitor] = []
    for pick in judged.competitors:
        c = by_id.pop(pick.id.strip(), None)  # pop: unknown and repeated IDs are both dropped
        if c is not None:
            out.append(Competitor(company=c, reason=pick.reason.strip()))
    return out[:MAX_COMPETITORS]

B3 is merged to `main`, pushed, and ticked in `TODO.md`. All 68 backend tests pass and `ruff` is clean. It hasn't been run against real Gemini yet: `.env` has no `GEMINI_API_KEY` and no `GEMINI_MODEL_FAST`. I added that pending check to `notes/B.md`.

What `find_competitors(company)` in `backend/core/competitors.py` does:
- **Candidates:** it takes the store's candidate list and removes the company itself.
- **Judging:** it asks Gemini (fast model, temperature 0, structured output) for up to 15 direct competitors, each with a one-line reason. The instructions say that sharing an industry isn't enough and that investors and suppliers never count.
- **Checks on Gemini's answer:** any ID that isn't a candidate, repeats, or is the company itself is dropped. Results keep Gemini's order and are capped at 15.
- **No candidates:** it returns an empty list without calling Gemini.

`similarity` is always empty for now. It gets a value once Agent A adds vector search (A13).

The fixtures only have 9 candidates per company, so the planned 10–15 can't be reached on the fake data. If Gemini is down or not configured, the function raises an error instead of falling back to the unjudged candidates. Without a key, the founder report can't be built for real.

import pytest

from contracts.schemas import Competitor
from core.conflict import check_conflict
from data import get_store

KELLUU = "78d7490a-dd04-5119-a7f1-e940b861219b"
STENDR = "3afdc63c-b992-4b25-b69d-807ab346352d"
NIF = "2ca07622-990d-40bf-a4fe-36434d43d6db"  # NATO Innovation Fund: led Kelluu's Series A
MAKI = "415bc278-6ed1-4973-a684-07a8b8c5d855"


@pytest.fixture
def store(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("USE_FAKE_STORE", "true")
    get_store.cache_clear()
    yield get_store()
    get_store.cache_clear()


async def rivals(store, *ids):
    return [Competitor(company=await store.company(i), reason="test") for i in ids]


async def test_portfolio_conflict_with_sources(store):
    out = await check_conflict(NIF, await rivals(store, KELLUU, STENDR))
    assert [(c.kind, c.competitor.id) for c in out] == [("PORTFOLIO", KELLUU)]
    assert out[0].competitor.name.startswith("Kelluu")
    assert out[0].sources and len(out[0].sources) == len(set(map(repr, out[0].sources)))


async def test_no_conflict_when_competitor_not_in_portfolio(store):
    assert await check_conflict(MAKI, await rivals(store, KELLUU)) == []


async def test_no_competitors_or_unknown_investor(store):
    assert await check_conflict(NIF, []) == []
    assert await check_conflict("unknown-investor", await rivals(store, KELLUU)) == []

B4 is merged to `main`, pushed, and ticked in `TODO.md`. All 71 backend tests pass and `ruff` is clean.

`check_conflict(investor_id, competitors)` in `backend/core/conflict.py` takes the investor's portfolio from the store and keeps the companies that are also in the competitor list. It returns one `PORTFOLIO` conflict per competitor, with the sources from the portfolio links (duplicates removed). No Gemini calls are involved.

The tests run on the fixture data:
- NATO Innovation Fund gets a conflict with Kelluu, which is in its portfolio.
- Maki.vc gets no conflict against Kelluu.
- An empty competitor list or an unknown investor returns no conflicts.

I didn't add any alias handling. Agent A's fixture builder already rewrites a company's alternate Cala IDs to its main ID, and no portfolio link in the fixtures uses an alternate ID. Agent A's real store needs to do the same, or conflicts will be missed silently. That's worth checking at the real-data pass (B9).

Next is **B5 (board conflicts)**, which adds `BOARD` conflicts to the same function. Want me to continue?

"""check_conflict (B4 PORTFOLIO, B5 BOARD): does an investor have a stake in a direct competitor?

Plain set logic over store data; every Conflict carries the sources of the edges it rests on.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio

from contracts.schemas import Competitor, Conflict, EntityRef, Source
from data import get_store


def _ref(c: Competitor) -> EntityRef:
    co = c.company
    return EntityRef(id=co.id, name=co.name, type=co.type, description=co.description)


def _union(*lists: list[Source]) -> list[Source]:
    out: list[Source] = []
    for sources in lists:
        out += [s for s in sources if s not in out]
    return out


async def check_conflict(investor_id: str, competitors: list[Competitor]) -> list[Conflict]:
    """PORTFOLIO: the investor's portfolio holds a competitor (one Conflict per competitor).
    BOARD: a competitor's BOARD member is one of the investor's people (one per competitor+person).
    """
    store = get_store()
    portfolio, investor_people = await asyncio.gather(
        store.portfolio(investor_id), store.people(investor_id)
    )
    by_id = {c.company.id: c for c in competitors}

    portfolio_hits: dict[str, Conflict] = {}
    for link in portfolio:
        comp = by_id.get(link.company.id)
        if comp is not None:
            new = Conflict(kind="PORTFOLIO", competitor=_ref(comp))
            hit = portfolio_hits.setdefault(comp.company.id, new)
            hit.sources = _union(hit.sources, link.sources)

    ours: dict[str, list[Source]] = {}  # investor's person id -> sources of their link to it
    for link in investor_people:
        ours[link.person.id] = _union(ours.get(link.person.id, []), link.sources)

    board: list[Conflict] = []
    if ours:  # nobody at the investor -> no BOARD conflict possible, skip the lookups
        their_people = await asyncio.gather(*(store.people(c.company.id) for c in competitors))
        for comp, links in zip(competitors, their_people, strict=True):
            seen: set[str] = set()
            for link in links:
                pid = link.person.id
                if link.role == "BOARD" and pid in ours and pid not in seen:
                    seen.add(pid)
                    board.append(
                        Conflict(
                            kind="BOARD",
                            competitor=_ref(comp),
                            via_person=link.person,
                            sources=_union(link.sources, ours[pid]),
                        )
                    )
    return [*portfolio_hits.values(), *board]

Plain set logic over store data; every Conflict carries the sources of the edges it rests on.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio

from contracts.schemas import Competitor, Conflict, EntityRef, Source
from data import get_store


def _ref(c: Competitor) -> EntityRef:
    co = c.company
    return EntityRef(id=co.id, name=co.name, type=co.type, description=co.description)


def _union(*lists: list[Source]) -> list[Source]:
    out: list[Source] = []
    for sources in lists:
        out += [s for s in sources if s not in out]
    return out


async def check_conflict(investor_id: str, competitors: list[Competitor]) -> list[Conflict]:
    """PORTFOLIO: the investor's portfolio holds a competitor (one Conflict per competitor).
    BOARD: a competitor's BOARD member is one of the investor's people (one per competitor+person).
    """
    store = get_store()
    portfolio, investor_people = await asyncio.gather(
        store.portfolio(investor_id), store.people(investor_id)
    )
    by_id = {c.company.id: c for c in competitors}

    portfolio_hits: dict[str, Conflict] = {}
    for link in portfolio:
        comp = by_id.get(link.company.id)
        if comp is not None:
            new = Conflict(kind="PORTFOLIO", competitor=_ref(comp))
            hit = portfolio_hits.setdefault(comp.company.id, new)
            hit.sources = _union(hit.sources, link.sources)

    ours: dict[str, list[Source]] = {}  # investor's person id -> sources of their link to it
    for link in investor_people:
        ours[link.person.id] = _union(ours.get(link.person.id, []), link.sources)

    board: list[Conflict] = []
    if ours:  # nobody at the investor -> no BOARD conflict possible, skip the lookups
        their_people = await asyncio.gather(*(store.people(c.company.id) for c in competitors))
        for comp, links in zip(competitors, their_people, strict=True):
            seen: set[str] = set()
            for link in links:
                pid = link.person.id
                if link.role == "BOARD" and pid in ours and pid not in seen:
                    seen.add(pid)
                    board.append(
                        Conflict(
                            kind="BOARD",
                            competitor=_ref(comp),
                            via_person=link.person,
                            sources=_union(link.sources, ours[pid]),
                        )
                    )
    return [*portfolio_hits.values(), *board]

I pulled first, which brought in Agent A's Cala client (A3). Then I did B5: it's merged to `main`, pushed, and ticked in `TODO.md`. All 88 backend tests pass and `ruff` is clean.

`check_conflict` in `backend/core/conflict.py` now finds both kinds of conflict:
- **PORTFOLIO:** unchanged from B4.
- **BOARD:** someone sits on a competitor's board and is also one of the investor's people. That gives one conflict per competitor and person, naming the person in `via_person`. The sources come from both links: the person's board seat and their tie to the investor.
- **Fewer lookups:** if the investor has no known people, it skips looking up the competitors' people. That avoids extra Cala calls on the real store.

The fixtures contain no real BOARD case: none of the investors' people sit on a competitor's board. So the BOARD tests use a stub that adds Kelluu's board member to Maki.vc's people. A second test checks that a shared person who is only the CEO doesn't count. It's not proven on real data yet; that comes at the real-data pass (B9).

Next is **B6 (scoring)**, which is unblocked now that B3 and B4 are done. It follows the Pitch/Skip split already recorded in `notes/B.md`. Continue?

B6 is merged to `main`, pushed, and ticked in `TODO.md`. All 157 backend tests pass (this includes Agent A's A4 work, which came in during the rebase) and `ruff` is clean. But the counter-drone conflict demo still won't work: on the current data interface, Stendr's backers never reach the Skip list.

**The demo gap (needs the three of you).** Investors can only reach Skip through a competitor's funding rounds, because our data interface (`DataStore`) has no "who invested in company X" lookup. Only 4 companies have round data in the fixtures, and Stendr isn't one of them. So Rainfall and Skyfall Ventures, Stendr's backers, never show up when the founder is Sensofusion. That breaks the conflict moment in the demo, and B8's "counter-drone conflict detected" check.
- **Proposal:** add `backers(company_id) -> list[PortfolioLink]` to `DataStore` and bump the contract to 1.2.0. Agent A's fixture builder already has this logic (`graph.backers()`), and my side is about 3 lines.
- The contract is frozen, so all three humans need to agree. Details are in `notes/B.md`.

**How `rank_investors(company, competitors=None)` in `backend/core/scoring.py` works:**
- **Who gets considered:** everyone in funding rounds of the competitive space, meaning the direct competitors plus the similar candidates. Added to that are the top 20 co-investors of the company's current investors, capped to stay within Cala's call limit.
- **Skip:** anyone with a conflict. Taking part in a direct competitor's funding round also counts as a portfolio conflict, citing that round, in case Cala's portfolio data is incomplete.
- **Score (0–100):** made of leads in the space (35), rounds in the space (20), how recently they last led a round (25) and warm intros (20). The weights sit in one dict at the top of the file.
- **Reasons:** every reason carries sources.

On the fixtures with Stendr as the company:
- Maki.vc tops Pitch at 73, having led the Aavuus and Metaktik pre-seeds.
- NATO Innovation Fund is in Skip as Kelluu's lead investor.

Two decisions I made that you may want to overrule:
- **Current investors are left out of both lists.** Otherwise Kelluu's own investors showed up in its Pitch list as "co-invested with your investor". Agent A's sample report does the same.
- **Warm-intro reasons have no sources.** Cala's co-investor data doesn't come with any.

Next is **B7: wire the founder and investor routes** to this code. It's unblocked and doesn't depend on the backers decision. Should I go ahead, and do you want to take the `backers()` proposal to the team?

import json

import pytest
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from api.main import app
from contracts.schemas import CONTRACT_VERSION, AgentEvent, Brief, FounderReport, InvestorCheck
from data import get_store

KELLUU = "78d7490a-dd04-5119-a7f1-e940b861219b"
SENSOFUSION_ALIAS = "5c699806-0fea-4e62-a594-717d4d85516c"
MAKI = "415bc278-6ed1-4973-a684-07a8b8c5d855"
STENDR = "3afdc63c-b992-4b25-b69d-807ab346352d"


@pytest.fixture
def client(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("USE_FAKE_STORE", "true")
    get_store.cache_clear()
    yield TestClient(app)
    get_store.cache_clear()


def events(resp) -> list[AgentEvent]:
    assert resp.headers["content-type"].startswith("text/event-stream")
    chunks = [c for c in resp.text.split("\n\n") if c]
    assert all(c.startswith("data: ") for c in chunks)
    return [AgentEvent.model_validate(json.loads(c[6:])) for c in chunks]


def test_health(client):
    assert client.get("/api/health").json() == {"ok": True, "contract_version": CONTRACT_VERSION}


def test_resolve(client):
    refs = client.post("/api/resolve", json={"name": "Kelluu", "kind": "company"}).json()
    assert KELLUU in [r["id"] for r in refs]


def test_founder_report_with_alias(client):
    r = client.post("/api/founder/analyze", json={"company_id": SENSOFUSION_ALIAS})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    FounderReport.model_validate(r.json())


def test_investor_check_and_brief(client):
    pair = {"investor_id": MAKI, "company_id": STENDR}
    InvestorCheck.model_validate(client.post("/api/investor/check", json=pair).json())
    Brief.model_validate(client.post("/api/brief", json=pair).json())


def test_slush_prep_stream(client):
    body = {"company_id": KELLUU, "investor_names": ["Maki.vc"]}
    job_id = client.post("/api/slush-prep", json=body).json()["job_id"]
    assert events(client.get(f"/api/jobs/{job_id}/stream"))[-1].type == "done"

content.text:
B7 is merged to `main`, pushed, and ticked in `TODO.md`. All 186 backend tests pass, `ruff` is clean, and local `main` matches GitHub. Agent A pushed A8 and A9 mid-merge, so I rebased twice. One push again hit GitHub's intermittent "remote rejected… failed", and the next push carried both commits.

What changed in the API:
- **`/api/founder/analyze`** now builds the report with the real scoring code. Without `competitor_ids`, Gemini judges the competitors; the result is kept in memory per company, so repeat calls (and investor checks for the same company) don't call Gemini again. With `competitor_ids`, it ranks against exactly those companies, deduplicated and without the company itself. Competitors already judged keep Gemini's reason. Any new one gets the reason "Chosen by you".
- **`/api/investor/check`** returns the investor, the company, the conflicts, the competitors and the funding rounds of the company and each competitor.
- **Errors:** an unknown ID returns 404. If Gemini isn't available, these routes return 503 with an `{error}` that says why.
- **Still on fixture samples:** `/api/brief`, slush prep and chat (until B11 and B13–B14).

Without a `GEMINI_API_KEY`, founder analyze and investor check will return that 503, so C should stay on the mock until the key arrives. The tests use a fake judge.

Agent A's latest note says Cala's graph is missing Tesi's investment in NestAI and flags that as a demo risk. It may be worth reading in `notes/A.md`.

Next is **B8, the eval set**: test cases built on the known demo facts. Note that the counter-drone conflict case will fail until the `backers()` contract change is agreed. Should I write it with that case marked as an expected failure, so it flips to passing once the data is there?

- `backers()` added to `DataStore` in `contracts/schemas.py`, plus the version bump to 1.2.0

- later, the same method on the real store (A8 already reads incoming relationships on companies, so it's a small step)

# Fixtures — demo cases (task T3)

Picked by the team on 13 Nov. Task A1 records raw Cala responses for these into `raw/`; task A2
builds contract models from them into `models/` (file list: `contracts/api.md` → Fixtures).
`models/index.json` holds the Cala IDs. Always use IDs, never names, as keys.

## Founder mode — 3 companies

| Company | Why |
| --- | --- |
| **Kelluu** (Finland, ISR airships, Series A) | Best-covered case: Series A led by NATO Innovation Fund, with Keen Venture Partners, Gungnir Capital and Tesi. Shows "who leads in your space". |
| **Sensofusion** (Finland, counter-drone) | Counter-drone set: its rivals' backers land on the Skip list. |
| **Nordic Air Defence** (Sweden, counter-drone) | Counter-drone set, second viewpoint on the same rivals. |

## Investor mode — 2 pairs (fund + startup that pitched)

| Fund | Startup | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Tesi** | **NestAI** (Finland, defence AI) | Tesi backs both Kelluu and NestAI: a live portfolio overlap for the conflict moment. |
| **Maki.vc** | **Stendr** (Norway, counter-drone) | Maki.vc leads defence pre-seeds (Aavuus, Metaktik); Stendr competes with Sensofusion and Nordic Air Defence. |

## Counter-drone set (the conflict moment)

Sensofusion, Stendr, Nordic Air Defence. Any investor behind one of them is a conflict for the
other two.

## Investors to record (~10)

NATO Innovation Fund, Keen Venture Partners, Gungnir Capital, Tesi, Maki.vc, Inventure, plus the
investors that appear in the rounds of the five companies above.

## Known traps

- Cala often has two entries for one firm, a `Company` and an `Organization` (e.g. "Kelluu Oy" and
  "Kelluu", two "Maki.vc"s). The one with funding rounds and investors attached is the right one.
- Name search is fuzzy: "Nordic Air Defence" also returns a UK shell company and Thales Air Defence.
- There are several unrelated "Inventure"s and "Tesi"s; the investors are the Finnish ones.

## Coverage found while recording (A1, 13 Nov)

- **Nordic Air Defence has no company entity in Cala** (only text answers). It cannot be a
  founder-mode company, so **Stendr is the third founder-mode sample** (agreed with the team).
- **Sensofusion** has an entity but no rounds or investors attached. It works as the company a
  founder enters; it adds no backers to anyone's Skip list.
- **NestAI** has one investor edge and no rounds in the graph; `sourced_answer()` knows its round.
- Details and the other findings: `notes/A.md`.

## Rebuilding

```sh
python -m data.record_fixtures   # raw/: calls Cala (about 10 calls a minute), skips what exists
python -m data.build_fixtures    # models/: rebuilt from raw/, no network
```

Never edit `raw/` or `models/` by hand. A test fails if `models/` is not what
`build_fixtures` produces from `raw/`.

"""B8 eval set: known facts about the demo cases (contracts/fixtures/README.md) the logic must find.

Runs on whatever `get_store()` returns: the fake store by default, live Cala with
USE_FAKE_STORE=false (B9). Competitors are fixed per case so scoring and conflicts are judged
without Gemini; the Gemini judge has its own case, skipped while GEMINI_API_KEY is empty.
"""

import os
from datetime import date

import pytest

from contracts.schemas import Competitor, FounderReport
from core.competitors import find_competitors
from core.conflict import check_conflict
from core.scoring import rank_investors
from data import get_store

KELLUU = "78d7490a-dd04-5119-a7f1-e940b861219b"
SENSOFUSION = "202e9283-6455-486f-8868-03c7e0d0cf29"
STENDR = "3afdc63c-b992-4b25-b69d-807ab346352d"
NESTAI = "14359613-a45f-4804-892d-3b9dd9e927a9"
NIF = "2ca07622-990d-40bf-a4fe-36434d43d6db"  # NATO Innovation Fund
MAKI = "415bc278-6ed1-4973-a684-07a8b8c5d855"
TESI = "df5be140-d50e-4e21-bb4f-d8f1e4ad3959"
STENDR_BACKERS = {
    "0322aa66-c3c7-470c-a940-e6ec117d4051",  # Rainfall Ventures
    "9b65ed62-ad4b-4a91-a9f8-f9bb6ae3b5b0",  # Skyfall Ventures
    "3ef31033-ce41-4b62-9aa5-f0eea1d58d07",  # Startuplab Founders
}
TODAY = date(2026, 11, 13)


@pytest.fixture
def store():
    get_store.cache_clear()  # pick up USE_FAKE_STORE from the environment / .env
    yield get_store()
    get_store.cache_clear()


async def founder(store, company_id: str, *rivals: str) -> FounderReport:
    competitors = [Competitor(company=await store.company(i), reason="eval") for i in rivals]
    return await rank_investors(await store.company(company_id), competitors, today=TODAY)


def by_id(report: FounderReport):
    return {s.investor.id: s for s in report.pitch + report.skip}


async def test_kelluu_series_a_lead_is_nato_innovation_fund(store):
    """Kelluu's Series A was led by NIF: for a Kelluu rival, NIF is a Skip with a known lead."""
    nif = by_id(await founder(store, STENDR, KELLUU, SENSOFUSION))[NIF]
    assert nif.conflicts and nif.conflicts[0].competitor.id == KELLUU
    assert nif.leads_in_space >= 1 and nif.lead_data in ("known", "partial")
    assert nif.last_lead_date and nif.last_lead_date.startswith("2026")
    assert any("Led" in r.text and r.sources for r in nif.reasons)


async def test_maki_leads_defence_pre_seeds(store):
    """Maki.vc led the Aavuus and Metaktik pre-seeds: a top Pitch for a defence startup."""
    report = await founder(store, KELLUU, STENDR, NESTAI)
    maki = by_id(report)[MAKI]
    assert not maki.conflicts and maki in report.pitch[:3]
    assert maki.leads_in_space >= 2
    assert any("Pre-Seed" in r.text and r.sources for r in maki.reasons)


async def test_tesi_backs_kelluu_conflict_for_rival(store):
    """Tesi backs Kelluu: checking Tesi for a Kelluu rival shows a sourced PORTFOLIO conflict."""
    rivals = [Competitor(company=await store.company(KELLUU), reason="eval")]
    conflicts = await check_conflict(TESI, rivals)
    assert [(c.kind, c.competitor.id) for c in conflicts] == [("PORTFOLIO", KELLUU)]
    assert conflicts[0].sources


@pytest.mark.xfail(
    strict=True,
    reason="needs DataStore.backers() (contract 1.2.0): Stendr has no rounds, so its backers "
    "never reach the pool. Remove this marker with the B6 backers change.",
)
async def test_counter_drone_conflict(store):
    """The demo's conflict moment: Stendr's backers are Skip for Sensofusion."""
    report = await founder(store, SENSOFUSION, STENDR, KELLUU)
    skipped = {s.investor.id: s for s in report.skip}
    hits = STENDR_BACKERS & set(skipped)
    assert hits

import asyncio, time, os
from data.config import load_env; load_env()
from agent.llm import structured
from pydantic import BaseModel
class A(BaseModel):
    answer: int
QS=[("Smallest positive integer n such that n! ends in exactly 100 zeros?",405),
    ("How many integers from 1 to 1000 are divisible by 3 or 5 but not by 15?",401),
    ("How many integers from 0 to 999 have decimal digit sum exactly 10?",63),
    ("How many ways to tile a 2x10 rectangle with 1x2 dominoes?",89),
    ("Number of trailing zeros of 2026! ?",503),
    ("How many positive divisors does 10! have?",270)]
async def run(m):
    os.environ["GEMINI_MODEL_FAST"]=m
    t=time.time()
    res=await asyncio.gather(*(structured(q,A,retries=2) for q,_ in QS), return_exceptions=True)
    ok=[(not isinstance(r,Exception)) and r.answer==a for r,(q,a) in zip(res,QS)]
    return m, sum(ok), round(time.time()-t,1), [getattr(r,'answer',str(r)[:40]) for r in res]
async def main():
    for r in await asyncio.gather(*(run(m) for m in ["gemini-4-argon","gemini-4-carbon","gemini-4-hydrogen","gemini-3.8-flash"])): print(r)
asyncio.run(main())
EOF

"""find_competitors (B3): the store's candidates, judged by Gemini down to the direct competitors.

Gemini only picks among candidate IDs and writes a one-line reason; any ID it invents is dropped.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from pydantic import BaseModel

from agent.llm import structured
from contracts.schemas import Company, Competitor
from data import get_store

MAX_COMPETITORS = 15

SYSTEM = """You judge which companies are DIRECT competitors of a startup, for a founder deciding \
which investors to pitch (an investor who backed a direct competitor has a conflict).
A direct competitor sells a similar product or service to similar customers. Same broad industry \
alone is not enough; investors, funds, agencies and suppliers are never competitors.
Use only the descriptions given. Return at most 15, the most direct first; return fewer (or none) \
if fewer qualify. Use only IDs from the candidate list, copied exactly. Each reason is one short \
factual sentence on what overlaps, with no numbers, dates or names not in the descriptions."""


class _Pick(BaseModel):

Gemini is now live, on the strongest model I could identify rather than Flash. The fix is merged and pushed to `main`, and 218 tests pass, including the live Gemini check. The one skipped test is Agent A's, which needs a MongoDB test URI.

**What I changed:**
- **Model:** `.env` now has `GEMINI_MODEL_FAST` and `GEMINI_MODEL_SMART` both set to `gemini-4-hydrogen`, and the competitor judge asks for the smart tier.
- **Model choice is a best guess:** the names Argon, Carbon and Hydrogen don't say which Gemini 4 model is the top one. Hydrogen has the largest output limit, which usually marks the top tier. All three gave the same answers on my test cases, so it's a one-line swap in `.env` if you know the ranking. `gemini-2.5-pro` is no longer available to new users.
- **Judge prompt fixed:** the first run kept 0 of 9 candidates on every model, Flash and Gemini 4 alike. My prompt said "use only the descriptions", but Cala's are too thin; Sensofusion's is just "Finnish defense technology company". Gemini may now also use what it reliably knows about the named companies. It can still only pick from Cala's candidate IDs, and reasons may not contain numbers, dates, funding or investor names.

**Live result, end to end through the API (about 3 s):** for Sensofusion, Gemini picks Stendr ("Both develop counter-drone detection and defense platforms"). Skip then holds Rainfall, Skyfall and Startuplab with the Stendr conflict, and Pitch is led by Maki.vc. That's the demo's conflict moment working.

**Kelluu gets no direct competitors.** None of its 9 Cala candidates makes airships or aerial surveillance, so the founder report would have an empty Skip list. That's down to which candidates the data layer suggests, which is Agent A's area (A11 now, vector search in A13).

**For the team:** `.env` isn't committed, so the other clones need the same two model lines to run founder mode. Tell C that founder analyze and investor check now work on the real API, still on the fixture data.

I'm still blocked on A12 for B9. The options that don't need it are still the MCP server (B15) or the agent tools (B12).

## What Cala's data looks like (found while recording fixtures, 13 Nov)

- **Rate limit: about 10 calls a minute** on our key (429 after that, no `Retry-After` header).
  The recorder waits 6.5 s between calls. The real store must cache hard and batch carefully.
- **`knowledge_query` and `knowledge_search` take 20–80 s each.** A combined query (several
  countries and stages at once) fails with "too complex"; one query per country works.
- **One firm can have several Cala IDs** (a `Company` and an `Organization`, or one per data
  source): two "Kelluu", two "Maki.vc", two "Gungnir Capital", two "Redstone". The fixture
  builder folds same-name entries into one (`index.json` → `aliases`). The real store needs the
  same step (A6).
- **Rounds live on `FundingRound` entities.** `transaction_value` is a number with
  `transaction_value_units`; the lead is `is_lead: true` on the investor's edge to the round.
  Only the lead is marked, so the others are "not lead" when a lead exists and "unknown" otherwise.
- **Demo cases that are thin in Cala:**
  - *Nordic Air Defence* has no company entity (only text answers: pre-seed, $4.2M, SNÖ Ventures).
    Stendr is the third founder-mode sample instead (agreed with the human).
  - *Sensofusion* has an entity but no rounds or investors.
  - *NestAI* has one investor edge and no rounds; `knowledge_search` knows its €100M round
    co-led by Tesi and Nokia. Gaps like this are what `sourced_answer()` is for.

## For B

- `data.NotFound` is raised by `company(id)` for an unknown ID. The list methods return `[]`.
- Founder mode: every investor found through a *direct* competitor's round is, by definition, a
  conflict. The sample reports therefore rank investors from the wider candidate pool (the
  "space") and put those tied to a direct competitor on the Skip list. Your scoring needs some
  such split or the Pitch list is always empty.

## For B and C: undated rounds (A7, 13 Nov)

Cala often links an investor to a company (`INVESTED_IN`) without any round. So that code walking
`rounds()` still finds those investors, `rounds(company_id)` ends with one extra `Round` when such
investors exist: id `"<company_id>:backers"`, no `label`, `date` or amount, `is_lead` unknown, with
the sources of those links. Both the fake and the real store do this (Stendr has only this one).
B: count it as "backs the company", not as a dated deal. C: show it as "Investors (round details
not known)" rather than an empty round row.

## Demo risk: Tesi -> NestAI is not in the graph (A8, 13 Nov)

The planned investor-mode demo ("Tesi backs both Kelluu and NestAI") only half exists in Cala's
graph: Tesi -> Kelluu is an `INVESTED_IN` link, but Tesi -> NestAI is not (NestAI's only graph
investor is PostScriptum Ventures). Cala's text answer does say Tesi and Nokia co-led NestAI's
EUR 100M round. So `portfolio(Tesi)` will not contain NestAI. The Tesi x NestAI check still shows
a conflict, through Kelluu as NestAI's competitor. To show "Tesi holds NestAI" itself, B has to
use `sourced_answer()`.

`portfolio()` on the real store is Cala's `INVESTED_IN` links only (one call). Deals that exist
only as rounds are in `investor_rounds()`.

- **A10: not yet checked against live MongoDB Atlas** (`MONGODB_URI` is empty). The cache passes

async def _org(self, entity_id: str) -> dict:
        """A company's or investor's retrieval. NotFound if the ID is something else."""
        entity = await self.cala.entity(
            entity_id,
            properties=list(_ORG_FIELDS.properties),
            outgoing=list(_ORG_FIELDS.outgoing),
            incoming=list(_ORG_FIELDS.incoming),
            limit=_EDGE_LIMIT,
        )
        if entity.get("entity_type") not in ORG_TYPES:
            kind = entity.get("entity_type") or "unknown type"
            raise NotFound(f"{entity_id} is not a company or an investor ({kind})")
        return entity

    async def _org_family(self, entity_id: str) -> tuple[str, list[dict]]:
        """The main ID and the retrievals of every entry of that firm, main one first."""
        main_id = self.canonical(entity_id)
        ids = [main_id, *self._siblings.get(main_id, [])]
        entities = await asyncio.gather(*[self._org(i) for i in ids])
        return main_id, list(entities)

    # --- DataStore -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

    async def investor_rounds(self, investor_id: str) -> list[Round]:
        """Rounds the investor took part in (up to 40), newest first. [] for an unknown ID."""
        try:
            main_id, entities = await self._org_family(investor_id)
        except NotFound:
            return []
        led: set[str] = set()
        ids: list[str] = []
        for entity in entities:
            for edge in related(entity, "outgoing", "PARTICIPATES_IN_FUNDING_ROUND"):
                properties = edge.get("properties") or {}
                if properties.get("role", "INVESTOR") != "INVESTOR":
                    continue
                ids.append(edge["id"])
                if properties.get("is_lead") is True:
                    led.add(edge["id"])
        rounds = await self._rounds(ids[:_MAX_INVESTOR_ROUNDS])
        result = []
        for item in rounds:
            if item.id in led:  # the investor's own edge says it led this round
                investors = [
                    i.model_copy(update={"is_lead": i.investor.id == main_id})
                    for i in item.investors
                ]
                item = item.model_copy(update={"investors": investors})
            if any(i.investor.id == main_id for i in item.investors):
                result.append(item)
        return result

    def _ref(self, raw: dict) -> EntityRef:
        """An EntityRef for an edge or a search hit, under the firm's main ID."""
        ref = map_entity_ref(raw)
        main_id = self.canonical(ref.id)
        return ref if main_id == ref.id else ref.model_copy(update={"id": main_id})

    async def _rounds(self, round_ids: list[str]) -> list[Round]:
        """Fetch and map funding rounds, newest first. Rounds Cala can't find are skipped."""
        unique = list(dict.fromkeys(round_ids))
        fetched = await asyncio.gather(
            *[
                self.cala.entity(
                    rid,
                    properties=list(_ROUND_FIELDS.properties),
                    incoming=list(_ROUND_FIELDS.incoming),
                    limit=_EDGE_LIMIT,
                )
                for rid in unique
            ],
            return_exceptions=True,
        )
        rounds = []
        for entity in fetched:
            if isinstance(entity, NotFound):
                continue
            if isinstance(entity, BaseException):
                raise entity
            mapped = map_round(entity)
            if mapped is None:

            investors: dict[str, RoundInvestor] = {}

Yes, it's been running about 18 minutes and is still going. What it's found so far:

- **Stendr resolves correctly** (`3afdc63c…`, the same ID as in the fixtures).
- **Gemini kept none of Stendr's real candidates as direct competitors.** I haven't printed the list yet. The likely cause is the same as Sensofusion: because Sensofusion has no industries, it never makes Stendr's candidate list either. So the counter-drone rival is missing from both sides, and the rest are probably broad aerospace or defence companies.
- **The slow part is the Cala rate limit.** With no direct competitors, the run is now fetching funding rounds for all of Stendr's candidates to build the Pitch list. That's about 200 live Cala calls so far, each waiting up to 10 minutes in the queue for the roughly 10-a-minute limit.

Only they, plus the direct rivals, feed the Pitch list; unrelated candidates are ignored. Real Stendr went from 49 SaaS funds in 21 minutes to an honest empty result in 5 seconds.

content.text:
Not this slow, no. Part of it is a hard external limit, but a good part is how many calls my scoring code makes.

**Why it's slow:** Cala allows about 10 calls a minute on our key, and the client queues calls to stay under that. So a cold run takes roughly (live calls ÷ 10) minutes: Stendr made 213 calls and took 21 minutes. Warm runs are near-instant: Agent A measured 0 s for a second Kelluu run, since everything is cached for 24 h.

**Where the calls go:**
- **Fixed cost:** about 2 candidate queries per country (20–80 s each), and one entity fetch per funding round of each company in the space.
- **My biggest cost: `investor_rounds()` for every investor in the pool.** Each one is a fetch of the investor plus up to 40 more, one per funding round, to work out "last lead date" and "deals in the last 12 months". With 30–50 investors that's most of the bill, and those two signals are worth at most 25 of the 100 points.

**What would fix it:**
1. **Mine, quick:** score everyone from the data already fetched, then call `investor_rounds()` only for the top ~10 Pitch candidates. My estimate is a 50–70% cut in cold calls. Skip-list investors don't need precise recency.
2. **Agent A:** set `MONGODB_URI` so the cache is shared through Atlas. Right now every clone starts cold and pays the same 20 minutes again.
3. **Agent A:** the batch job (A14/A15) already precomputes last lead and 12-month deals per investor in the graph. The data interface just has no method to read it, which would take a contract change.
4. **Ask Cala** at the workshop whether the hackathon key can get a higher rate limit.

For the demo itself the cache will be warm, so it'll be fast. But any company typed in live that isn't cached will take minutes. C already shows a "slow" notice for that.

Good news meanwhile: the live Kelluu run now finds real direct competitors, Aispeco and others ("autonomous aerial platforms… for ISR"). It's still fetching rounds, at 90 live calls so far.

Want me to do fix 1 now?
